name: Metformin
meal_timing: Take with or immediately after meals (breakfast/dinner)

avoid: Excessive alcohol (increases risk of lactic acidosis)
Crash starvation diets
caution: Taking on an empty stomach frequently causes nausea, cramps, and diarrhea
beneficial: Vitamin B12-rich foods (milk, curd, eggs, paneer, fortified nutritional yeast) to prevent B12 depletion
High-soluble-fiber foods (oats, barley, fenugreek/methi seeds, ragi) for glycemic stabilization

critical_alert: Avoid alcohol consumption. If taking for over 1-2 years, monitor Vitamin B12 levels regularly.
clinical_summary: Decreases hepatic glucose production and increases insulin sensitivity. Food slows absorption slightly but dramatically improves gastrointestinal tolerance.

name: Glimepiride
meal_timing: Take immediately before or with the first substantial meal of the day (usually breakfast)

avoid: Alcohol (severely escalates risk of sudden hypoglycemia)
Skipping meals
caution: Never take without eating a carbohydrate-containing meal shortly after; risk of dangerous hypoglycemic drops
beneficial: Complex unrefined carbohydrates (millets, oats, brown rice, whole wheat) for sustained glucose release
Carry fast-acting carbohydrates (dextrose tablets, raisins, fruit juice) for emergency hypoglycemic relief

critical_alert: High risk of hypoglycemia if meals are skipped or delayed. Always eat within 15-30 minutes of taking.
clinical_summary: Stimulates pancreatic beta-cells to secrete insulin. Must be synchronized with food intake to match insulin release with dietary carbohydrate absorption.

name: Gliclazide
meal_timing: Take with breakfast or morning meal

avoid: Alcohol
Skipping breakfast
caution: Do not crush or chew modified release (MR) formulations
beneficial: Fiber-rich breakfast (oats, sprouted moong, vegetable poha) to avoid rapid blood glucose spikes

critical_alert: Skipping meals while on Gliclazide can cause severe hypoglycemia.
clinical_summary: Second-generation sulfonylurea with selective pancreatic beta cell binding; reduces post-meal glycemic excursions when taken with breakfast.

name: Sitagliptin
meal_timing: May be taken with or without food at the same time each day

avoid: High-glycemic-index sugary foods, sweetened drinks, and refined pastries
caution: Excessive alcohol
beneficial: Low-GI vegetables, legumes, and lean proteins to support GLP-1 inkretin action

critical_alert: Low inherent risk of hypoglycemia on its own; risk increases if combined with sulfonylureas or insulin.
clinical_summary: Inhibits DPP-4 enzyme, prolonging endogenous active incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP) which stimulate glucose-dependent insulin release.

name: Dapagliflozin
meal_timing: Take in the morning with or without food

avoid: Severe dehydration, excessive alcohol (risk of ketoacidosis), very low-carbohydrate/keto diets without medical monitoring
caution: Diuretic effect: drink plenty of clean water throughout the day (at least 2-2.5 liters unless fluid restricted)
beneficial: Hydrating foods (cucumber, bottle gourd, buttermilk, clear vegetable soups)

critical_alert: Promotes urinary glucose excretion; maintain adequate hydration to prevent volume depletion, orthostatic hypotension, and urinary tract infections.
clinical_summary: Inhibits sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 in proximal renal tubules, reducing blood glucose and blood pressure while conferring cardioprotective and nephroprotective benefits.

name: Empagliflozin
meal_timing: Take once daily in the morning with or without food

avoid: Excessive alcohol
Extreme dehydration
caution: Ensure consistent daily water intake to balance mild osmotic diuresis
beneficial: DASH-diet foods, leafy greens, potassium-balanced vegetables

critical_alert: Maintain good hydration and genital hygiene to reduce risk of mycotic infections.
clinical_summary: Selectively blocks renal glucose reabsorption. Demonstrates proven reduction in cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization.

name: Pioglitazone
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food

avoid: Excessive dietary sodium (worsens fluid retention and peripheral edema)
caution: Watch for sudden weight gain or swelling in ankles/feet
beneficial: Low-sodium foods, fresh vegetables, potassium-rich foods to balance fluid equilibrium

critical_alert: Contraindicated in patients with symptomatic heart failure due to potential for fluid retention.
clinical_summary: Improves target cell response to insulin without increasing pancreatic insulin secretion; promotes adipocyte glucose uptake.

name: Amlodipine
meal_timing: Take once daily at the same time, with or without food

avoid: Grapefruit and Grapefruit juice (inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism, causing dangerously high drug levels and severe hypotension)
caution: Excessive dietary sodium (counteracts antihypertensive efficacy)
High alcohol intake
beneficial: Potassium-rich vegetables (spinach, ridge gourd, ash gourd) to naturally support endothelial vasodilation
Garlic, hibiscus tea, and dietary nitrate foods (beetroot) for synergistic blood pressure control

critical_alert: STRICT WARNING: Do NOT consume grapefruit, seville oranges, or pomelo juice while taking Amlodipine.
clinical_summary: Relaxes arterial smooth muscle by inhibiting calcium influx into vascular cells. Grapefruit blocks intestinal CYP3A4, multiplying systemic bioavailability unpredictably.

name: Telmisartan
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food at the same time each day

avoid: High-potassium salt substitutes (such as Lona, potassium chloride table salt substitutes) which can lead to life-threatening hyperkalemia
caution: Excessive dietary licorice (can raise BP)
Excess potassium supplements without blood monitoring
beneficial: DASH-diet plant foods with natural minerals, unrefined grains, berries, and moderate natural potassium
Low-sodium culinary seasonings (lemon juice, cumin, coriander, mint) instead of sodium salt

critical_alert: Do NOT use potassium-based salt substitutes or potassium supplements without consulting your doctor (risk of hyperkalemia).
clinical_summary: Selectively blocks AT1 receptor subtype, preventing angiotensin II-induced vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion. Conserves potassium in renal tubules.

name: Losartan
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food

avoid: Potassium-enriched salt substitutes
Excessive potassium dietary supplements
caution: Alcohol may cause dizziness or orthostatic hypotension
beneficial: Low-sodium dietary foods, antioxidant-rich vegetables, flaxseeds

critical_alert: Avoid potassium chloride salt alternatives. Monitor serum potassium and creatinine regularly.
clinical_summary: Competitive antagonist of angiotensin II receptors. Provides renal protection in type 2 diabetic nephropathy in addition to BP control.

name: Ramipril
meal_timing: Take with or without food, preferably at the same time every morning

avoid: Potassium salt substitutes (KCl)
Potassium supplements unless specifically prescribed
caution: High intake of dried fruits or potassium-dense juices if kidney function is compromised
beneficial: DASH diet staples: green vegetables, oats, lentils, and fresh fruits with natural moderate potassium

critical_alert: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, decreasing potassium excretion. Watch out for hyperkalemia.
clinical_summary: Suppresses renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system by inhibiting ACE. Slows progression of diabetic nephropathy and post-MI ventricular remodeling.

name: Enalapril
meal_timing: Take once or twice daily with or without food

avoid: Potassium chloride salt substitutes
caution: Dehydration or heavy sweating increases risk of hypotension
beneficial: Balanced hydration and low-sodium home cooked meals

critical_alert: Do not substitute normal salt with potassium-based 'low-sodium' salts without checking serum potassium.
clinical_summary: Prodrug bioactivated to enalaprilat, decreasing systemic vascular resistance and left ventricular afterload.

name: Metoprolol
default_dosage: 25 mg or 50 mg (Succinate ER or Tartrate)
meal_timing: Take with or immediately after a meal (food enhances bioavailability and systemic absorption)

avoid: Alcohol (may precipitate abrupt blood pressure drops and heightened dizziness)
caution: Caffeine and high-energy drinks (stimulants counteract bradycardic rate-control effects)
beneficial: Magnesium-rich foods (pumpkin seeds, almonds, spinach) to support normal cardiac rhythm

critical_alert: Never abruptly discontinue beta-blockers without physician supervision (risk of rebound tachycardia and hypertension).
clinical_summary: Cardioselective beta-1 adrenergic antagonist. Food significantly increases systemic bioavailability of metoprolol tartrate by reducing first-pass hepatic extraction.

name: Atenolol
meal_timing: Take once daily, preferably at the same time, with or without meals

avoid: Excessive alcohol
High amounts of orange juice consumed at the exact same moment (may mildly decrease absorption)
caution: Do not stop taking abruptly
beneficial: Heart-healthy Mediterranean and DASH foods, omega-3 rich walnuts and chia seeds

critical_alert: Do not skip doses. Monitor pulse rate before taking (hold if heart rate < 55 bpm unless cleared).
clinical_summary: Hydrophilic beta-1 blocker that slows heart rate, decreases myocardial contractility, and lowers blood pressure.

name: Furosemide
meal_timing: Take in the morning with a meal (to avoid sleep disruption from nocturia and minimize stomach irritation)

avoid: Excessive sodium/salty snacks (negates diuretic efficacy)
Heavy alcohol
caution: Furosemide causes heavy urinary loss of potassium and magnesium; hypokalemia is a frequent complication
beneficial: Potassium-rich foods (tender coconut water, bananas, oranges, spinach, potatoes, lentils) to replenish electrolyte losses
Magnesium-rich foods (seeds, whole grains)

critical_alert: Depletes bodily potassium and magnesium. Consume potassium-rich natural foods or supplements as advised by your physician.
clinical_summary: Inhibits Na-K-2Cl symporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle. Produces potent diuresis with marked excretion of sodium, chloride, potassium, and water.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
meal_timing: Take once daily in the morning with or without food

avoid: High sodium processed foods
Excessive black licorice (worsens hypokalemia)
caution: Causes mild potassium and magnesium loss; may slightly raise uric acid and blood glucose
beneficial: Potassium-containing fruits, vegetables, and hydrating broths

critical_alert: Take in the morning to prevent waking up at night to urinate. Monitor blood electrolytes periodically.
clinical_summary: Inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubules, producing modest diuresis and vasodilation.

name: Atorvastatin
meal_timing: Take once daily in the evening or bedtime, with or without food

avoid: Grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and Seville oranges (CYP3A4 inhibition elevates statin blood levels, drastically increasing risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis)
Heavy alcohol (increases hepatic strain)
caution: Do not take huge doses of oat bran or pectin simultaneously; space fiber supplements by 1-2 hours
beneficial: Soluble fiber foods (oats, isabgol/psyllium husk, fenugreek, apples, lentils) to synergistically reduce LDL-C
Omega-3 fatty acids (flaxseed, chia, walnuts, fish) and plant sterols

critical_alert: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Promptly report any unexplained muscle tenderness, weakness, or dark urine.
clinical_summary: Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis. Grapefruit compounds block CYP3A4-mediated hepatic clearance.

name: Rosuvastatin
meal_timing: Take once daily at any time of day, with or without food

avoid: Antacids containing aluminum and magnesium hydroxide within 2 hours of dosing (decreases absorption by 50%)
Excessive alcohol
caution: Less CYP3A4 dependent than atorvastatin, but moderation with grapefruit is still prudent
beneficial: Heart-healthy monounsaturated fats (mustard oil, olive oil), soluble fiber, and antioxidant vegetables

critical_alert: Space antacid medications by at least 2 hours. Report unexplained muscle aches or fatigue.
clinical_summary: Hydrophilic statin cleared primarily by CYP2C9 and biliary excretion. Demonstrates superior LDL-C lowering and HDL elevation efficacy.

name: Levothyroxine
meal_timing: STRICT REQUIREMENT: Take first thing in the morning on an EMPTY STOMACH with a full glass of plain water, at least 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast or morning tea/coffee

avoid: Taking with milk, tea, coffee, or breakfast (absorption drops by 40-60%)
Soy products (soybean, soy milk, tofu) and walnuts within 4 hours
Calcium-fortified drinks or supplements within 4 hours
Iron supplements (ferrous sulfate) within 4 hours
caution: High dietary fiber meals taken immediately after can trap thyroxine in the intestinal lumen
beneficial: Balanced nutritious meals with adequate selenium (mushrooms, sunflower seeds) and zinc after waiting 60 minutes post-dose

critical_alert: Must be taken on an empty stomach with plain water. Keep a minimum 4-hour gap between Levothyroxine and Calcium, Iron, Soy, or Dairy supplements.
clinical_summary: Synthetic crystalline L-tetraiodothyronine (T4). Bioavailability is heavily compromised by gastric pH alterations, divalent cations (Ca2+, Fe2+), caffeine, and dietary fibers.

name: Pantoprazole
meal_timing: Take 30 to 60 minutes BEFORE the morning meal (breakfast) on an empty stomach

avoid: Spicy, excessively greasy/fried foods, carbonated sodas, and late-night heavy meals that trigger acid reflux
Alcohol
caution: Long-term PPI use (>1 year) can reduce absorption of dietary Vitamin B12, Calcium, and Magnesium
beneficial: Soothing gut-friendly foods (plain yogurt/curd, coconut water, boiled oats, bananas, bottle gourd)
Foods rich in magnesium and calcium once meals resume

critical_alert: Must be swallowed whole 30-60 minutes before food so that drug peak coincides with activation of proton pumps by the meal.
clinical_summary: Irreversibly binds the H+/K+ ATPase pump in gastric parietal cells. Food stimulates pump translocation, hence timing before food is critical for optimal acid suppression.

name: Omeprazole
meal_timing: Take once daily in the morning 30-60 minutes before breakfast

avoid: Trigger foods: citrus juices, tomatoes, caffeine, chocolates, deep-fried snacks
caution: Do not open or crush enteric-coated capsules
beneficial: Non-acidic vegetables, rice porridge, stewed apples, chamomile or fennel tea

critical_alert: Take before your morning meal. Swallow whole with a glass of water.
clinical_summary: Potent inhibitor of basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion. Requires acidic gastric activation followed by covalent canalicular pump binding.

name: Aspirin (Low Dose)
meal_timing: Take WITH or immediately AFTER a meal with a full glass of water (never on an empty stomach)

avoid: Alcohol (significantly compounds gastric irritation and risk of severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding)
Massive megadoses of garlic, ginger, ginkgo biloba, or omega-3 fish oil supplements that compound antiplatelet activity
caution: Taking on an empty stomach frequently induces erosive gastritis and gastric mucosal ulceration
beneficial: Milk, curd, or a warm whole-grain meal before taking to coat the gastric mucosa

critical_alert: Always take with or after meals to protect your stomach lining. Do NOT consume alcohol with Aspirin.
clinical_summary: Irreversibly acetylates COX-1 in platelets, preventing thromboxane A2 synthesis. Direct mucosal contact and systemic PG inhibition can precipitate gastric mucosal injury without food.

name: Clopidogrel
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food at the same time every day

avoid: Excessive alcohol
Concomitant high doses of natural anticoagulants (vitamin E megadoses, high-dose feverfew)
caution: Avoid taking with Omeprazole concurrently unless prescribed, as Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 activation of Clopidogrel (Pantoprazole is preferred)
beneficial: Balanced diet with antioxidant vegetables and moderate healthy fats

critical_alert: Check with doctor before taking over-the-counter pain medications or herbal blood thinners.
clinical_summary: Thienopyridine prodrug bioactivated by CYP2C19 to inhibit ADP-induced platelet aggregation. Less gastrotoxic than aspirin, can be taken with or without food.

name: Warfarin
default_dosage: 2 mg, 3 mg, or 5 mg (as titrated by INR)
meal_timing: Take once daily in the evening, with or without food, at the exact same hour

avoid: Cranberry juice, pomegranate juice, and alcohol (can elevate INR dangerously)
Drastic sudden swings in dietary Vitamin K intake
caution: Do NOT suddenly start or stop eating large quantities of Vitamin K rich foods (spinach, kale, methi leaves, broccoli, cabbage). Keep your daily intake CONSISTENT
beneficial: Consistent, steady daily portions of green vegetables rather than extreme fluctuations

critical_alert: CRITICAL FOOD INTERACTION: Vitamin K directly opposes Warfarin. Keep your intake of green leafy vegetables steady from day to day.
clinical_summary: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase complex 1 (VKORC1), stopping gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X. Large fluctuations in dietary vitamin K destabilize anticoagulation.

name: Montelukast
meal_timing: Take once daily in the evening, with or without food

avoid: Alcohol (may increase drowsiness and sedation)
caution: None significant with general food
beneficial: Anti-inflammatory foods (turmeric/curcumin, ginger, warm soups, honey) to support bronchial health

critical_alert: Best taken in the evening to protect against nocturnal asthma and morning allergic rhinitis symptoms.
clinical_summary: Selective antagonist of cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptor. Inhibits bronchoconstriction, mucosal edema, and cellular inflammation.

name: Cetirizine
meal_timing: Take in the evening or bedtime with or without food

avoid: Alcohol and CNS depressants (causes severe drowsiness and impaired reflexes)
caution: Food slightly delays time to peak concentration (Tmax) but does not decrease total absorption
beneficial: Warm herbal teas (tulsi, ginger, peppermint) to soothe airway passages

critical_alert: Avoid driving or operating machinery if you experience drowsiness. Do not drink alcohol.
clinical_summary: Second-generation peripheral H1 receptor antagonist with minimal blood-brain barrier penetration, providing effective allergy relief with reduced central sedation.

name: Amoxicillin and Potassium Clavulanate
meal_timing: Take at the START of a meal or with food

avoid: Alcohol during antibiotic therapy
Skipping doses or stopping before full course is finished
caution: Clavulanic acid can cause diarrhea and nausea if taken on an empty stomach
beneficial: Probiotic foods (fresh homemade curd/yogurt, buttermilk) taken 2 hours apart from the antibiotic to replenish healthy gut microbiota
Hydrating fluids and easily digestible meals (khichdi, vegetable soup)

critical_alert: Take at the start of a meal to enhance absorption of clavulanate and prevent nausea and diarrhea. Complete full course.
clinical_summary: Co-administration with food enhances clavulanate absorption and optimizes gastrointestinal tolerability while amoxicillin bactericidal cell wall synthesis inhibition proceeds.

name: Ciprofloxacin
meal_timing: Take 2 hours before or 2 hours AFTER dairy products or mineral-rich meals

avoid: Taking directly with milk, yogurt, paneer, cheese, or calcium-fortified juices (calcium chelates the drug, reducing absorption by up to 90%)
Iron, zinc, or magnesium antacids/supplements taken simultaneously
caution: Caffeine (ciprofloxacin inhibits caffeine clearance, potentially causing tremors, palpitations, and insomnia)
beneficial: Plenty of water throughout the day to prevent crystalluria

critical_alert: DO NOT take with dairy products (milk, yogurt) or calcium/iron supplements. Keep a 2-hour window before and after.
clinical_summary: Polyvalent cations (Ca2+, Mg2+, Fe2+, Al3+) form insoluble coordination chelates with the 4-keto and 3-carboxyl groups of fluoroquinolones, preventing intestinal absorption.

name: Azithromycin
meal_timing: May be taken with or without food; taking with a light meal reduces stomach discomfort

avoid: Aluminum and magnesium antacids taken at the exact same time (reduces peak concentration)
caution: Avoid heavy greasy meals which may worsen nausea
beneficial: Yogurt/buttermilk spaced 2 hours apart to safeguard beneficial gut microflora

critical_alert: Take once daily at the same time. Complete full prescribed course (usually 3 to 5 days).
clinical_summary: Reversibly binds the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible microorganisms. Tablets have high oral bioavailability and tissue penetration.

name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
meal_timing: Can be taken with or without food (taking on an empty stomach acts faster; taking with food is gentler)

avoid: Alcohol (severely elevates risk of acute toxic hepatic necrosis / liver injury)
caution: Do not exceed maximum daily limit of 4000 mg (or 3000 mg in chronic use) across all combination products
beneficial: Warm hydration, light broths, electrolyte fluids, herbal teas

critical_alert: DO NOT drink alcohol while taking Paracetamol. Chronic alcohol consumption drastically increases liver toxicity risk.
clinical_summary: Acts primarily on central prostaglandin synthesis with minimal peripheral anti-inflammatory action. Concomitant ethanol induces CYP2E1, shunting metabolism into toxic NAPQI.

name: Ibuprofen
meal_timing: STRICTLY take WITH food, milk, or a meal (never on an empty stomach)

avoid: Alcohol (exponentially increases risk of stomach ulcers and GI bleeding)
caution: Excess sodium intake; NSAIDs can promote fluid retention and blunted BP control
beneficial: Warm milk, oats porridge, or a cooked meal before dose to coat gastric mucosa

critical_alert: Always take after food or with milk to protect your stomach lining from ulcers and erosions.
clinical_summary: Non-selective COX inhibitor. Depletes gastroprotective prostaglandins (PGE2, PGI2) in gastric mucosa. Food reduces peak contact irritation.

name: Calcium Carbonate + Vitamin D3
meal_timing: Take WITH meals (gastric acid produced during meals is essential to dissolve and absorb calcium carbonate)

avoid: Taking simultaneously with Levothyroxine, Ciprofloxacin, or Iron (space by at least 2 to 4 hours)
Excessive caffeine or carbonated cola beverages (increases urinary calcium excretion)
caution: High-oxalate foods (spinach, beet greens) eaten simultaneously can bind a portion of calcium, though overall diet is healthy
beneficial: Dairy products, fortified milk, sesame seeds (til), and sunlight exposure for natural vitamin D activation

critical_alert: Calcium carbonate REQUIRES stomach acid; take with meals. Keep a 4-hour gap from Levothyroxine and Iron supplements.
clinical_summary: Calcium carbonate requires acidic ionization for intestinal absorption via TRPV6 channels. Divalent Ca2+ binds thyroxine and fluoroquinolones into unabsorbable complexes.

name: Ferrous Ascorbate / Iron Supplement
meal_timing: Best taken on an empty stomach with a Vitamin C source (lemon water or amla juice) for maximum absorption, OR with a light snack if nausea occurs

avoid: Tea, coffee, green tea (tannins and polyphenols inhibit iron absorption by up to 75%)
Milk, cheese, yogurt, and calcium tablets (calcium competes directly for the DMT1 transporter) - space by 2 hours
High-phytate unfermented bran taken in the exact same mouthful
caution: Stools may turn dark green/black (harmless)
beneficial: Vitamin C foods (Indian gooseberry/amla, lemon, guava, sweet lime, capsicum) taken alongside iron drastically enhance bioavailability

critical_alert: Do NOT take iron with tea, coffee, milk, or calcium tablets. Pair with lemon water or amla for superior absorption.
clinical_summary: Ascorbate maintains iron in the soluble ferrous (Fe2+) state, facilitating uptake via divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1). Tannins, polyphenols, and calcium strongly inhibit uptake.

name: Valsartan
meal_timing: Take with or without food at the same time each day

avoid: Potassium-based salt substitutes
Excessive alcohol
caution: High potassium intake without doctor supervision
beneficial: Low-sodium DASH foods, leafy greens, antioxidant fruits

critical_alert: Avoid potassium chloride salt alternatives. Monitor serum potassium periodically.
clinical_summary: Angiotensin II receptor antagonist; reduces peripheral vascular resistance and preserves renal function.

name: Olmesartan
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food

avoid: Potassium chloride salt substitutes
caution: Severe prolonged diarrhea requires medical review (sprue-like enteropathy)
beneficial: Hydrating foods, low sodium home cooking

critical_alert: Do not take potassium supplements without consulting your doctor.
clinical_summary: Selective AT1 receptor blocker providing 24-hour sustained blood pressure control.

name: Lisinopril
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food

avoid: Potassium salt substitutes
Heavy alcohol
caution: High potassium diets can lead to hyperkalemia
beneficial: DASH diet meals with balanced natural minerals

critical_alert: May cause dry persistent cough. Avoid potassium salt alternatives.
clinical_summary: Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, suppressing angiotensin II formation and lowering systemic vascular resistance.

name: Carvedilol
meal_timing: Take WITH food to minimize the risk of orthostatic hypotension and dizziness

avoid: Alcohol (increases risk of orthostatic dizziness and fainting)
caution: Large amounts of caffeine may diminish blood pressure lowering
beneficial: Balanced heart-healthy meals rich in magnesium and omega-3s

critical_alert: Always take with food to slow absorption rate and reduce orthostatic blood pressure drops.
clinical_summary: Dual alpha-1 and beta-adrenergic antagonist with antioxidant properties; indicated in heart failure, hypertension, and post-MI.

name: Bisoprolol
meal_timing: Take once daily in the morning with or without food

avoid: Excessive alcohol
caution: Do not stop abruptly without doctor supervision
beneficial: Low-sodium meals and moderate physical activity

critical_alert: Do not skip doses. Check heart rate periodically before taking.
clinical_summary: Highly selective beta-1 blocker reducing cardiac workload and myocardial oxygen consumption.

name: Nebivolol
category: Cardiovascular (Third-Generation Beta-1 Blocker with Nitric Oxide Vasodilation)
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food

avoid: Alcohol
Energy drinks with high caffeine
caution: May mask hypoglycemia tremors in diabetic patients
beneficial: Dietary nitrate rich foods (beetroot, spinach) to support endothelial NO production

critical_alert: Possesses unique nitric oxide donating properties causing peripheral vasodilation.
clinical_summary: Highly cardioselective beta-1 blocker that stimulates endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS), reducing peripheral vascular resistance.

name: Propranolol
meal_timing: Take before meals or with food consistently

avoid: Alcohol
Caffeine in excess
caution: Protein-rich meals increase its bioavailability; keep meal composition consistent
beneficial: Magnesium-rich seeds and calming herbal teas

critical_alert: Contraindicated in asthma and severe COPD (can precipitate severe bronchospasm).
clinical_summary: Non-selective beta-1 and beta-2 adrenergic antagonist; useful in angina, tremors, migraine prophylaxis, and portal hypertension.

name: Diltiazem
meal_timing: Take before meals and at bedtime, or as prescribed with water

avoid: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice (potentiates diltiazem levels)
Alcohol
caution: Do not crush extended-release tablets
beneficial: Heart-healthy DASH diet meals with moderate natural minerals

critical_alert: Avoid grapefruit. Inhibits CYP3A4 enzyme, causing interactions with numerous cardiovascular drugs.
clinical_summary: Benzothiazepine calcium channel blocker; slows AV node conduction, decreases heart rate, and dilates coronary and systemic arteries.

name: Verapamil
meal_timing: Take with meals or milk to avoid stomach upset

avoid: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice (massively increases verapamil concentrations)
Alcohol
caution: Constipation is common: increase dietary fiber and water intake
beneficial: High-fiber vegetables, oats, prunes, and adequate hydration

critical_alert: AVOID GRAPEFRUIT. Strong inhibitor of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein.
clinical_summary: Phenylalkylamine CCB with pronounced negative inotropic and dromotropic actions. Highly effective in supraventricular tachycardias.

name: Cilnidipine
meal_timing: Take once daily in the morning with or after breakfast

avoid: Grapefruit juice
Excessive sodium
caution: Sudden position changes if feeling lightheaded
beneficial: Low-sodium meals, fresh vegetables, garlic

critical_alert: Dual L/N-type blocker with lower incidence of pedal edema and sympathetic activation compared to amlodipine.
clinical_summary: Blocks both L-type and N-type voltage-dependent calcium channels, suppressing sympathetic overactivity and renal afferent/efferent arteriolar constriction.

name: Spironolactone
meal_timing: Take with food or breakfast (food enhances bioavailability and minimizes gastric irritation)

avoid: Potassium chloride salt substitutes (can cause fatal hyperkalemia)
Potassium supplements or high-dose potassium drinks without monitoring
caution: Excessive consumption of dried fruits, bananas, tender coconut water if serum potassium is high
beneficial: Low-sodium wholesome home-cooked meals

critical_alert: POTASSIUM-SPARING: Strictly avoid potassium salt substitutes. High risk of hyperkalemia when combined with ACEIs or ARBs.
clinical_summary: Competitive aldosterone receptor antagonist in the distal renal tubule; increases sodium and water excretion while retaining potassium and hydrogen ions.

name: Chlorthalidone
meal_timing: Take in the morning with food

avoid: Excessive sodium snacks
Heavy alcohol
caution: Causes mild potassium loss; monitor serum electrolytes
beneficial: Potassium-balanced vegetables and fresh fruits

critical_alert: Long half-life (>40 hours). Preferred thiazide-like diuretic in AHA/ACC hypertension guidelines.
clinical_summary: Inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the early distal tubule; long terminal elimination half-life delivers sustained 24h BP reduction.

name: Digoxin
meal_timing: Take once daily with water; meals high in bran fiber should be spaced by 2 hours

avoid: Simultaneous high-fiber meals (e.g. oat bran, psyllium husk can bind digoxin and reduce absorption)
Black licorice (glycyrrhizin induces hypokalemia, precipitating fatal digoxin toxicity)
caution: Hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia dramatically potentiates digitalis toxicity
beneficial: Consistent potassium intake to safeguard normal myocardial sensitivity

critical_alert: NARROW THERAPEUTIC INDEX: Hypokalemia triggers severe arrhythmias. Report nausea, visual halos, or slow irregular pulse immediately.
clinical_summary: Inhibits myocardial Na+/K+ ATPase, increasing intracellular calcium and cardiac contractility while slowing AV nodal conduction.

name: Amiodarone
meal_timing: Take with meals consistently (food significantly enhances oral absorption)

avoid: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice (inhibits CYP3A4 and increases amiodarone levels to toxic ranges)
caution: St. John's wort
High iodine seaweed supplements
beneficial: Heart-healthy balanced diet

critical_alert: EXTREME DDI RISK: Inhibits CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, and P-gp. Doubles blood levels of Digoxin, Warfarin, and Statins.
clinical_summary: Multichannel blocker with predominant potassium outward rectifier inhibition (Class III); highly lipophilic with extensive tissue distribution.

name: Glipizide
meal_timing: Take 30 minutes BEFORE the first meal of the day (breakfast)

avoid: Alcohol
Skipping or delaying meals after taking
caution: Always have a carbohydrate-containing meal within 30 minutes
beneficial: Complex carbohydrates (millets, whole oats, lentils) to avoid hypoglycemic troughs

critical_alert: Must be taken 30 minutes before food for optimal timing of insulin peak with food absorption.
clinical_summary: Rapidly absorbed sulfonylurea that stimulates early phase insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells.

name: Vildagliptin
meal_timing: May be taken with or without food

avoid: High-sugar confectionaries, sugar-sweetened sodas
caution: Excessive alcohol
beneficial: Low glycemic index Indian staples (ragi, sprouted moong, green leafy vegetables)

critical_alert: Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) periodically as per clinical guidelines.
clinical_summary: Potent and selective dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor; enhances both alpha- and beta-cell responsiveness to glucose.

name: Linagliptin
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food at any time

avoid: Refined sugars and syrups
caution: Hypoglycemia risk if combined with insulin or sulfonylurea
beneficial: Balanced fiber-rich diet; safe in kidney disease without dose reduction

critical_alert: Does not require dose adjustment in renal impairment (cleared primarily via bile and gut).
clinical_summary: Xanthine-based DPP-4 inhibitor with primarily non-renal route of excretion; highly convenient in diabetic kidney disease.

name: Teneligliptin
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without breakfast

avoid: Sugary sweets, jaggery in excess, packaged juices
caution: Alcohol
beneficial: Vegetable salads, methi paratha (whole wheat), curd, roasted chana

critical_alert: Widely prescribed cost-effective DPP-4 inhibitor in India with convenient once-daily dosing.
clinical_summary: Features a unique J-shaped structure that anchors into the S1, S2, and S2-extensive sub-sites of DPP-4 for potent, long-lasting inhibition.

name: Canagliflozin
meal_timing: Take once daily BEFORE the first meal of the day

avoid: Dehydration
Excess alcohol
Extreme ketogenic diet
caution: Maintain daily fluid intake (2-3 liters water unless fluid restricted)
beneficial: Hydrating foods (cucumber, bottle gourd, coconut water) and DASH diet

critical_alert: Dual SGLT2 and mild intestinal SGLT1 inhibition; taking before breakfast delays intestinal glucose absorption.
clinical_summary: Inhibits SGLT2 in kidneys and SGLT1 in intestine; reduces blood glucose, HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, and body weight.

name: Semaglutide
meal_timing: ORAL STRICT RULE: Take on an empty stomach upon waking with no more than 120 ml (half glass) of plain water. Wait AT LEAST 30 MINUTES before eating, drinking, or taking other oral medications

avoid: Eating or drinking anything within 30 minutes of taking oral tablet (absorption drops to near zero)
Greasy, fried, and very fatty foods which exacerbate nausea, vomiting, and delayed gastric emptying
caution: Eat smaller, lighter portions to avoid fullness and GI distress
beneficial: Small protein-rich meals, broths, and easily digestible whole foods

critical_alert: ORAL RYBELSUS REQUIREMENT: Swallow whole with half glass plain water. Absolutely no food, beverage, or other meds for 30 minutes.
clinical_summary: Long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist; stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying, and reduces appetite.

name: Voglibose
meal_timing: STRICT REQUIREMENT: Take immediately with the VERY FIRST BITE of each main meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner)

avoid: Taking after a meal (ineffective once food has been digested)
Treating hypoglycemia with table sugar/sucrose (voglibose blocks sucrose digestion; MUST use pure GLUCOSE/dextrose powder or tablets)
caution: High-starch meals may produce mild flatulence and abdominal distension
beneficial: Indian carbohydrate staples (roti, rice, dal) are digested more slowly and evenly

critical_alert: Must be taken with the first bite of food. In case of hypoglycemia, treat ONLY with pure Glucose (Dextrose), NOT cane sugar.
clinical_summary: Reversibly inhibits alpha-glucosidase enzymes in the small intestine brush border, delaying carbohydrate cleavage into simple monosaccharides.

name: Repaglinide
meal_timing: Take within 15 minutes BEFORE each main meal (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner)

avoid: Alcohol (severe hypoglycemia)
Skipping meals (if you skip a meal, SKIP the dose!)
caution: Do not take if unable to eat immediately after
beneficial: Regular structured meals with complex carbs and protein

critical_alert: RULE: If a meal is skipped, skip the dose. If an extra meal is added, add a dose.
clinical_summary: Nonsulfonylurea secretagogue; closes ATP-dependent potassium channels in beta cells with rapid onset and short duration for postprandial control.

name: Insulin Glargine
meal_timing: Inject once daily subcutaneously at the EXACT same time every day, independent of meals

avoid: Alcohol (blunts counterregulatory glucose response causing delayed severe hypoglycemia)
caution: Keep daily carbohydrate distribution consistent
beneficial: Steady low-GI meal schedules

critical_alert: Do NOT mix with other insulins in the same syringe. Always carry fast-acting glucose for emergencies.
clinical_summary: Recombinant human insulin analogue with glycine/arginine substitutions; micro-precipitates in subcutaneous tissue for flat, peakless 24h basal release.

name: Fenofibrate
meal_timing: Take with meals (food significantly enhances bioavailability)

avoid: Heavy alcohol (exacerbates hypertriglyceridemia and pancreatitis risk)
caution: Watch for muscle pain if co-administered with statins
beneficial: Omega-3 rich foods (walnuts, flaxseed, fish) and low-refined-sugar diet

critical_alert: Primary agent for severe hypertriglyceridemia (>500 mg/dL) to prevent acute pancreatitis.
clinical_summary: Activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-alpha), stimulating lipoprotein lipase and reducing apolipoprotein C-III.

name: Gemfibrozil
meal_timing: Take 30 minutes BEFORE morning and evening meals

avoid: Alcohol
Concurrent statin therapy (severely contraindicated)
caution: High fat meals right before dose reduce absorption
beneficial: Low-saturated fat, low-simple-carbohydrate diet

critical_alert: CONTRAINDICATED WITH STATINS: High risk of severe rhabdomyolysis and acute renal failure. Fenofibrate is preferred.
clinical_summary: Inhibits peripheral lipolysis and hepatic triglyceride synthesis. Strongly inhibits statin glucuronidation and OATP1B1 uptake.

name: Ezetimibe
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food, at any time of day

avoid: High-cholesterol, high-trans-fat foods
caution: Bile acid sequestrants (cholestyramine) reduce absorption; space by 2-4 hours
beneficial: Plant sterols, oats, soluble fiber to synergistically lower LDL-C

critical_alert: Selectively inhibits the NPC1L1 transporter in the jejunal brush border, reducing dietary cholesterol absorption by 54%.
clinical_summary: NPC1L1 cholesterol absorption inhibitor; produces 15-20% further LDL-C reduction when added to statin therapy.

name: Esomeprazole
meal_timing: Take at least 1 hour BEFORE eating on an empty stomach

avoid: Spicy, oily, acidic, caffeinated food and sodas
Alcohol
caution: Long-term use may impair B12, Magnesium, and Calcium absorption
beneficial: Soothing alkaline foods (curd, coconut water, bananas, boiled vegetables)

critical_alert: S-isomer of omeprazole with higher systemic bioavailability. Take 60 min before breakfast.
clinical_summary: Inhibits H+/K+-ATPase in gastric parietal cells, suppressing stimulated and basal gastric acid secretion.

name: Sucralfate
meal_timing: Take on an EMPTY STOMACH 1 hour before meals and at bedtime

avoid: Taking simultaneously with food (binds dietary proteins and becomes ineffective)
Taking antacids within 30 minutes before or after (needs mild acid to form protective polymer gel)
caution: Binds almost all oral medications; keep at least a 2-HOUR GAP between sucralfate and other drugs
beneficial: Bland, non-irritating diet while ulcer heals

critical_alert: BINDS MEDICATIONS: Keep at least a 2-hour interval between Sucralfate and any other oral prescription drugs.
clinical_summary: Aluminum salt of sucrose octasulfate; polymerizes in acidic milieu to form a sticky viscous paste that adheres to ulcer craters.

name: Escitalopram
meal_timing: Take once daily in the morning or evening, with or without food

avoid: Alcohol (exacerbates sedation, dizziness, and cognitive impairment)
caution: NSAID pain relievers taken concurrently increase stomach bleed risk
beneficial: Tryptophan-containing whole foods (bananas, oats, nuts) and calming chamomile tea

critical_alert: Do NOT take with Tramadol or MAOIs (risk of Serotonin Syndrome). Combines with NSAIDs to increase bleed risk.
clinical_summary: Pure S-enantiomer of citalopram; highly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor with minimal dopamine or norepinephrine affinity.

name: Pregabalin
meal_timing: Take with or without food at consistent times (often at bedtime to reduce daytime dizziness)

avoid: Alcohol (massively increases drowsiness, respiratory depression, and ataxia)
caution: High fat meals mildly delay absorption but do not alter total bioavailability
beneficial: Balanced anti-inflammatory diet (turmeric, nuts, green leafy vegetables) for nerve health

critical_alert: First-line therapy for painful Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy. Avoid alcohol.
clinical_summary: Binds alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels in the CNS, reducing calcium influx and presynaptic release of excitatory neurotransmitters.

name: Gabapentin
meal_timing: Take with water, with or without food (taking with food may decrease stomach upset)

avoid: Alcohol
caution: Antacids containing aluminum and magnesium reduce gabapentin absorption by 20%; space by 2 hours
beneficial: B-complex vitamin rich foods (curd, nuts, whole grains) for peripheral nerve support

critical_alert: Space antacid intake by at least 2 hours. Common for diabetic neuropathy.
clinical_summary: Modulates calcium channels via alpha-2-delta subunit; actively transported across the gut wall by the LAT1 amino acid transporter.

name: Allopurinol
category: Antigout / Uric Acid Lowering (Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitor)
meal_timing: Take immediately AFTER meals with plenty of fluids (at least 2-2.5 liters of water daily)

avoid: Alcohol (especially beer, which is rich in purines and inhibits uric acid excretion)
High-purine foods (organ meats, red meats, sardines, shellfish, excessive yeast extracts)
High-fructose corn syrup and heavily sweetened beverages
caution: Adequate hydration is essential to prevent renal xanthine stones
beneficial: Cherries, vitamin C-rich amla and citrus, low-fat dairy products, and lots of water

critical_alert: Drink 2 to 3 liters of water daily. Stop and report immediately if skin rash or itchiness develops.
clinical_summary: Purine analogue that competitively inhibits xanthine oxidase, preventing the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid.

name: Febuxostat
category: Antigout / Uric Acid Lowering (Non-purine Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitor)
meal_timing: Take once daily with or without food

avoid: Beer, spirits, high-purine organ meats, sugar-sweetened sodas
caution: Hydrate well
beneficial: Alkaline vegetables, fresh fruits, curd, and adequate water intake

critical_alert: More potent non-purine xanthine oxidase inhibitor safe in allopurinol-sensitive individuals.
clinical_summary: Selectively blocks both oxidized and reduced forms of xanthine oxidase, achieving profound and sustained serum urate reduction.

name: Fluconazole
meal_timing: May be taken with or without food

avoid: Alcohol
caution: Potent CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 inhibitor
beneficial: Hydrating fluids

critical_alert: MAJOR DDI CULPRIT: Strongly inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4. Can cause severe hypoglycemia with Sulfonylureas and bleeding with Warfarin.
clinical_summary: Inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase; concurrently inhibits mammalian cytochrome P450 enzymes CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4.

name: Clarithromycin
meal_timing: Take with or without food (taking with food reduces metallic taste and nausea)

avoid: Grapefruit juice
Alcohol
caution: Do not combine with statins like Atorvastatin or Simvastatin
beneficial: Probiotic foods spaced 2 hours apart

critical_alert: POTENT CYP3A4 INHIBITOR: Strictly contraindicated with Atorvastatin/Simvastatin (extreme risk of fatal rhabdomyolysis).
clinical_summary: Binds 50S ribosomal subunit; potently inactivates CYP3A4, causing massive accumulation of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates.

name: Metronidazole
meal_timing: Take WITH or immediately after meals with plenty of water

avoid: ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: ALCOHOL in any form during therapy and for 48 hours after stopping
Alcohol-containing cough syrups or mouthwashes
caution: Produces severe disulfiram-like reaction (violent vomiting, flushing, tachycardia, chest pounding)
beneficial: Easily digestible bland meals (khichdi, curd rice)

critical_alert: STRICT ALCOHOL BAN: Consuming even small amounts of alcohol causes severe violent vomiting and tachycardia (disulfiram reaction).
clinical_summary: Generates toxic reactive nitro radical intermediates in anaerobic organisms; inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, preventing acetaldehyde breakdown.

name: Diclofenac
meal_timing: Take WITH or immediately after food or with a glass of milk

avoid: Alcohol (exponentially increases gastric bleeding and ulceration risk)
Excessive sodium
caution: Blunts effectiveness of ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics
beneficial: Warm cooked meals, milk, curd to coat gastric mucosa

critical_alert: Always take after food. Co-administration with Aspirin, Blood thinners, or ACE inhibitors/Diuretics carries major risks.
clinical_summary: Potent COX-1 and COX-2 inhibitor; reduces prostaglandin-mediated inflammatory pain while depleting cytoprotective gastric mucus.

name: Tramadol
meal_timing: Take with or without food

avoid: Alcohol (life-threatening respiratory depression and profound sedation)
caution: Do not combine with antidepressants (Escitalopram) or other serotonergic drugs
beneficial: High-fiber foods and adequate fluids to prevent opioid-induced constipation

critical_alert: Avoid alcohol. Combining with SSRIs (Escitalopram) or SNRIs significantly increases risk of Seizures and Serotonin Syndrome.
clinical_summary: Mu-opioid receptor agonist with dual inhibition of serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake; lowers seizure threshold.
